Lessons.Title: Inverses and Radical Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original section skills: invert polynomial and rational functions, restrict non-one-to-one polynomial domains, invert radicals, analyze composed radical-rational domains and apply inverse models.
An inverse reflects ordered pairs across y=x. Always compare the original domain with the inverse range.
For quadratic inverses, impose the original increasing or decreasing branch before choosing the sign of a square root.
For radical or rational expressions, keep the original exclusions; clearing denominators and squaring may introduce invalid candidates.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: (a) invert f(x)=(x+2)² on x≥−2; (b) invert f(x)=√(x−4)+3; (c) find domain of √((x−1)/(x+2)).
Independent Try It 1: For f(x)=x³−5, write f⁻¹ and verify by composition.
Independent Try It 2: Find inverse of f(x)=(x+1)² on x≥−1.
Independent Try It 3: Find inverse of f(x)=(x−2)² on x≤2.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse functions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Interchange inputs and outputs; an inverse function exists if the original is one-to-one on its stated domain.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Verify both compositions and exchange domain/range.

KeyConcepts.Title: Restricted quadratic inverse
KeyConcepts.Definition: A full parabola is not one-to-one; restrict to one monotone branch.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The original branch determines ±√ after swapping x and y.

KeyConcepts.Title: Radical inverse
KeyConcepts.Definition: Undo the radical with squaring/cubing, but preserve range and domain restrictions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Squaring may introduce extraneous roots; always check against original range.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse rational functions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Swap x,y then solve linearly for x; exclude denominator zeros in original and inverse.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check impossible horizontal-asymptote outputs are not in inverse domain.

KeyConcepts.Title: Radical rational domains
KeyConcepts.Definition: A square root requires nonnegative radicand and nonzero original denominator.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use a sign chart of numerator zeros and denominator poles.

Visuals.Title: Inverse function ordered pairs
Visuals.Description: Independent reflection table; swap inputs and outputs.

SummaryPoints: Interpret inverse models with physical units.
Cool-down reviews a restricted quadratic inverse, a radical inverse, and real-radicand sign restrictions.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use both square-root branches for a single inverse function.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Without an original domain restriction a parabola is not one-to-one.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Choose branch based on the restricted original domain.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ignore radical output constraints when inverting.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Squaring can introduce invalid extraneous cases.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Record inverse domain from original range and check.
